title: pr-70418-probabilistic-recall-smokecheck-and-explainable-failure-reporting.json
author: Aisha Gupta
release_notes: Add probabilistic recall-based smokecheck for prompt-sets with explainable failure artifacts; new CI hook triggers on statistically significant recall regression and uploads per-prompt exemplars for triage.
body: Context and motivation: We observed recurring silent regressions in recall-sensitive prompt-sets where aggregate accuracy held steady but the model dropped recovery on low-frequency positive examples. Existing SLOs focus on precision-like metrics and mean scores; this PR implements a probabilistic recall smokecheck tailored for prompt-sets and augments failing runs with explainable artifacts to speed triage. Design summary: Introduces a new metric, CalibratedRecall, that computes per-cohort recall with bootstrap-based 95% confidence intervals and a hierarchical smoothing prior to stabilize small cohorts. The CI gate triggers only when the delta from the baseline exceeds the configured threshold and the bootstrap interval excludes zero. On failure the hook assembles an explainable-failure bundle containing: top-k false-negative exemplars, nearest-counterfactual prompts (simple edit-distance and paraphrase sampling), model token-level logits for the exemplar responses, and prompt metadata (cohort, tags, input-length). These artifacts are packaged and uploaded to the internal eval-artifacts S3 bucket with a stable prefix for automatic linking in incident pages. Rollout and behavior: The smokecheck is wired as an opt-in CI hook for the eval pipeline and as a default guard on main regression jobs; it defaults to non-blocking for small datasets but blocks (CI fail) when sample-size>=200 and the calibrated delta>3% with 95% CI. For large prompt-sets the hook respects cohort-priority weighting to avoid noisy failures from tiny cohorts. Implementation details: - New code under eval-harness/metrics/calibrated_recall.py implements the bootstrap estimator, hierarchical prior, and cohort weighting. - CI hook: eval-harness/ci/hooks/probabilistic_recall_hook.py integrates with existing eval orchestration and artifacts uploader. - Reporting: eval-harness/reporting/explainable_bundle.py creates the artifact tarball and JSON manifest. - Tests: unit tests and deterministic bootstrap smoke tests under tests/metrics/test_calibrated_recall.py and tests/ci/test_prob_recall_hook.py. - Docs: brief docstring and a CI-runbook note in docs/ci/README-eval-hooks.md. Testing and validation: Added deterministic unit tests with seeded bootstraps and a small synthetic dataset to validate false-positive rate. Ran the new smokecheck against historical baselines in the backfill harness: no-significant-failures on 13 historical runs, and reproduced the regression in ENG-4521 dataset. Performance: The bootstrap adds ~1.2s per 1k examples in the smoke runner; artifact packaging is async and uses streaming upload to avoid blocking the main runner. Backwards compatibility: Default config keeps the hook disabled for legacy jobs; settings exposed via CI env flags and eval config. Migration notes: Ops should add eval-artifacts write-role to CI runner if not present.
commits_summary: 3 commits: (1) Implement calibrated recall estimator and CLI integration (Aisha Gupta) (2) Add CI hook and artifacts uploader with integration tests (Aisha Gupta) (3) Docs and minor test flakiness fixes; small follow-up to address reviewer comments.
review_thread: Julian Park: Nice work, the bootstrap approach looks reasonable but we should guard against seed sensitivity and ensure deterministic logs for CI reproductions.Aisha: Added deterministic seeding and an option to dump the random state into the artifact manifest for reproducibility.Marta Ivanova: Can we reduce the noise for cohorts with <50 examples? The hierarchical prior helps but we might need a floor to avoid spurious CI failures.Aisha: Implemented cohort-priority weighting and added sample-size floor default=30; documented behavior. Also added backfill validation against historical runs.Ethan Cole: CI failure on first run: packaging step timed out uploading 18MB artifact.Aisha: Increased streaming chunk size and switched to multipart upload in the hook; re-ran and all CI checks passed. Approvals: Julian approved after minor comments; Marta left LGTM after the floor change; Ethan approved post CI fix.
ci_summary: Initial CI run failed in artifact upload (timeout) but unit tests and bootstrap smoke tests were green. After switching to multipart streaming upload and re-running the pipeline all checks passed: unit, integration, lint, packaging. Final status: pass. Hook added to nightly eval and gated on main with opt-in flag and a non-blocking default for small datasets.
merge_summary: Merged via squash on 2026-02-20 by Aisha Gupta. Merge method: squash and merge. Post-merge actions: Updated internal runbook with hook configuration, granted eval-artifacts write-role to CI runner, scheduled a canary run against the 3 high-priority prompt-sets next nightly run.
notes: This PR is intentionally conservative: the gate defaults to non-blocking for small samples and includes explicit flags for teams to opt into stricter enforcement. The explainable bundle format is versioned (v1) to allow future additions without breaking the automated triage pipeline.
